criteria.text: Count the words, lines and characters in a text file
List the most frequent words
Print the results as JSON for other programs
Read standard input when the file is given as -
Report a missing file as an error
Run as python -m wordstats <file> from the project directory. It prints three lines: words: <n>, lines: <n> and characters: <n>
A word is a run of letters, digits and apostrophes. characters counts every character, newlines included. lines is the number of lines; a last line without a newline still counts
--top N prints the N most frequent words instead, one per line as <word> <count>, most frequent first, ties in alphabetical order. Words are compared in lower case
--json prints {"words": n, "lines": n, "characters": n}, or with --top N prints {"top": [{"word": w, "count": c}, ...]}
A file that does not exist prints an error to standard error and exits with status 2
Counts are exactly as the interface defines them
The top words are ordered as the interface says
JSON output parses and matches the plain output
Errors go to standard error with exit status 2

rulings.stands: The specification does not write this file.
rulings.gives_way: Checks if the file path exists using try/except FileNotFoundError. If not found, prints f"Error: '{path}' not found\n" to sys.stderr and returns 2.
rulings.why: The setup decides that the harness writes and keeps acceptance/conftest.py, so the product specification cannot dictate its internal logic or existence beyond what the harness provides.

rulings.stands: Returns the string.; returns: str: Compact JSON string with no extra whitespace and no trailing newl
rulings.gives_way: AC-7: Character count includes newlines; line count includes a final line even if it lacks a trailing newline.
rulings.why: The brief specifies JSON output as structured data for programmatic consumption, implying standard JSON formatting without trailing newlines, whereas the trailing newline rule in AC-7 applies to text line counting logic, not the JSON serialization format.

rulings.stands: format_plain_top return value (str): One line per top word formatted as '{word} {count}\n'. No trailing newline after the last entry is NOT added — each entry includes its own newline.
rulings.gives_way: AC-7: Character count includes newlines; line count includes a final line even if it lacks a trailing newline.
rulings.why: The specification explicitly defines the output format for plain top words as having each entry terminated by a newline, which is a formatting contract distinct from the file content counting rules in AC-7.

criteria.text: Create a note with a title and a body
List all notes
Fetch one note by its id
Update a note's title and body
Delete a note
Notes survive a restart of the service
JSON over HTTP. A note is {"id": <integer>, "title": <string>, "body": <string>}
POST /notes with {"title": ..., "body": ...} creates a note and answers 201 with the note
GET /notes answers 200 with a JSON array of every note
GET /notes/{id} answers 200 with the note, or 404 when there is none
PUT /notes/{id} with {"title": ..., "body": ...} replaces both and answers 200 with the note, or 404
DELETE /notes/{id} answers 204, or 404
A title that is missing or empty is refused with 400 or 422, and nothing is stored
GET /health answers 200
The project directory has a start.sh that starts the service on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the PORT environment variable, keeping its data under the directory in the DATA_DIR environment variable
Every operation works as the interface says
Notes persist across restarts
Invalid input is refused without storing anything

rulings.stands: - Response on success: 204 No Content with no response body; the note is permanently removed from the data file
rulings.gives_way: Component 5: Acceptance Tests (acceptance/*.spec.js) — Uses Playwright request fixture to test full HTTP endpoints against a running service instance. Starts the service via child_process.exec or similar mechanism, waits for GET /health to return status 200 before any test runs, sends HTTP requests with appropriate methods and bodies, asserts on status codes and response body shapes.
rulings.why: The brief explicitly defines DELETE /notes/{id} as returning 204, so the API contract defining the response body takes precedence over the generic test description which allows asserting on shapes that must match the API.

rulings.stands: - Response on success: 204 No Content with no response body; the note is permanently removed from the data file
rulings.gives_way: src/app.js — DELETE /notes/{id} handler(req, res): Parses {id} path parameter using parseId(). If invalid, responds with 400 Bad Request and JSON error body {"error": "<message>"}. Reads notes via readNotes(). Finds the note index matching the ID. If not found, responds with 404 Not Found and JSON error body {"error": "<message>"}. Removes the note from the array. Calls writeNotes() to persist. Re
rulings.why: The brief mandates a 204 status for successful deletion, which by definition has no body; the function contract's implication of returning a body for success contradicts the API contract and brief.

rulings.stands: - Request: GET /health with no body and no path parameters
rulings.gives_way: Path parameters for /notes/{id} are strictly validated as positive integers; decimals, non-numeric strings, zero, and negatives return 400.
rulings.why: These statements refer to different endpoints (/health vs /notes/{id}); there is no contradiction, but the finding incorrectly identifies them as opposing views on the same parameter scope.

rulings.stands: - Request: GET /notes with no body and no path parameters
rulings.gives_way: Path parameters for /notes/{id} are strictly validated as positive integers; decimals, non-numeric strings, zero, and negatives return 400.
rulings.why: These statements refer to different endpoints (/notes vs /notes/{id}); there is no contradiction, but the finding incorrectly identifies them as opposing views on the same parameter scope.

rulings.stands: Acceptance tests use Playwright's request fixture against a running service instance started via start.sh with explicit PORT and DATA_DIR environment variables.
rulings.gives_way: {"title": "PORT environment variable requirement", ... "decision": "start.sh exits with non-zero code if PORT is not set in the environment. No default port is used."}
rulings.why: The brief requires PORT from the environment variable, so the acceptance tests must provide it explicitly; the decision confirms no default is used, meaning the tests' explicit provision is required and consistent with the decision.

rulings.stands: monolog/monolog ^3.7 — Import: use Monolog\Logger; use Monolog\Handler\RotatingFileHandler; use Monolog\Level. Call: $logger = new Logger('notes-api'); $logger->pushHandler(new RotatingFileHandler(DATA_DIR . '/notes-api.log', 30, Level::Debug)); $logger->info('Request received', ['method' => 'POST', 'path' => '/notes', 'status' => 201]); Logs HTTP method, path, status code, and request duration.
rulings.gives_way: notes-api/src/Middleware/JsonBodyMiddleware.php — Slim middleware that parses the raw request body as JSON, sets parsed body on the request attributes, and rejects non-JSON or oversized bodies (over 1 MB) with HTTP 400.
rulings.why: The first statement incorrectly assigns Monolog logging functionality to the JSON body middleware, whereas the brief mandates logging via Monolog as a separate concern.

rulings.stands: GET /notes — Request: no body. Response: 200 OK with body <JSON array of note objects> where each element is {"id": <integer>, "title": <string>, "body": <string>}. Returns empty array [] when no notes exist.
rulings.gives_way: TS-2 (List Notes): Given N notes exist, when I GET /notes, then the response status is 200 and the JSON array length is N with each element having fields id, title, body.
rulings.why: The first statement covers all cases including empty results as required by the brief, while the second only describes the non-empty case.

rulings.stands: Request body content (title, body) is excluded from Monolog log output to prevent accidental leakage of user-provided note text into log files. Only HTTP method, path, status code, and request duration are logged.
rulings.gives_way: GET /notes/{id} (Fetch): Client sends GET request with integer ID in path. GetNoteHandler parses ID, creates NoteId::from() (validates > 0). Calls PdoNoteRepository::findById(). Repository executes SELECT * WHERE id = ?. If found, returns Note; else null. Handler returns 200 with note JSON or 404 with error JSON.
rulings.why: The second statement correctly addresses the privacy constraint regarding log content, which is a specific requirement from the brief, whereas the first describes standard data flow without addressing the logging exclusion.

rulings.stands: The service binds to 127.0.0.1 (localhost only) by default via the HOST environment variable or its 127.0.0.1 default, preventing external network access.
rulings.gives_way: No external network connectivity is required or used by the service. All processing and storage are local.
rulings.why: The second statement implements the brief's explicit requirement for the service to listen on 127.0.0.1.

rulings.stands: AC-1: POST /notes with valid {"title":"Test","body":"Content"} returns status 201 and response body contains id (integer), title ("Test"), body ("Content").
rulings.gives_way: AC-5/AC-12: Create a note via POST /notes, DELETE /notes/{id}, assert status 204 (no response body); then GET /notes/{id} to confirm it returns 404; also DELETE an id that does not exist asserting 404.
rulings.why: The second statement correctly reflects the brief's requirement that POST /notes returns a 201 status with the created note in the response body.
